chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Marhum al-Azdi, who said:
I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام say:

Whoever fasts the first day of Sha'ban, Paradise becomes absolutely obligatory for him. Whoever fasts two days, Allah looks at him every day and night in the abode of this world, and He continues His gaze upon him in Paradise. And whoever fasts three days, Allah visits him on His Throne from His Paradise every day.

key_terms.الْجَنَّةُ: Paradise, the promised reward mentioned in the hadith.
key_terms.دَارِ الدُّنْيَا: The abode of this worldly life.
key_terms.زَارَهُ اللَّهُ: Allah visits him, an expression of exalted divine favor as stated in the narration.
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: The month of Sha‘ban, in which the fast mentioned here is observed.
key_terms.نَظَرَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ: Allah turns His regard toward him, expressing divine favor and mercy.

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fasting the first days of Sha‘ban according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith encourages fasting in the opening days of Sha‘ban by describing immense divine reward for fasting one, two, or three days. It emphasizes the spiritual rank of voluntary fasting and links devotion in this world to nearness, divine regard, and Paradise in the hereafter.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1824 - It is narrated by al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Marhoom al-Azdi, who said:
"I heard Abu Abdullah (Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)) say:
'Whoever fasts the first day of Sha‘ban, Paradise becomes absolutely obligatory for him. Whoever fasts two days, Allah (swt) looks at him every day and night in this world and continues His gaze upon him in Paradise. And whoever fasts three days, Allah (swt) visits him on His Throne in His Paradise every day.'"
